subject.title: fix(skills): enforce byte-level cap on skill package downloads

question: Should dependency download limits follow verified ClawHub install provenance, or should every skill metadata download receive the 256 MiB cap regardless of workspace origin?
rationale: Filesystem source classification cannot distinguish a default ClawHub-installed workspace skill from a user-authored local workspace skill, so choosing between provenance-aware enforcement and a compatibility-breaking global cap requires maintainer security and product intent.

options.title: Use install provenance
options.body: Carry existing ClawHub origin/tracking metadata into installer selection and cap registry-origin dependency downloads without changing genuinely local workspace behavior.

options.title: Cap every download installer
options.body: Apply the 256 MiB cap to all metadata download specs and explicitly accept that existing larger local or custom downloads will fail.

options.title: Pause the hardening
options.body: Do not merge until the repository has a durable provenance fact or an explicitly approved global compatibility policy.

recommendation.title: Use install provenance
recommendation.body: Carry existing ClawHub origin/tracking metadata into installer selection and cap registry-origin dependency downloads without changing genuinely local workspace behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal spans both the ClawHub lifecycle and infra download boundary where the permanent policy needs to be owned.
